environment.description: Same Spring Boot application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate behind ALB. Session credentials are managed by a sidecar container running HashiCorp Vault Agent (v1.15.x) with a custom template that rotates the session signing key material every 60 seconds via Vault's transit/secrets engine with a TTL of 60s on the wrapping token. The Spring session store is backed by Redis ElastiCache (cluster mode) with a custom SessionRepository implementation that validates session tokens against the current and previous (grace window) Vault-issued HMAC. When a CSRF attack is crafted, the attacker must reference a valid JSESSIONID; however, the session HMAC rotates every 60 seconds and the Redis session entry is re-keyed atomically. The attacker's stolen/observed session cookie becomes cryptographically invalid within 60 seconds because the HMAC verification uses the rotated key. Additionally, the Vault Agent sidecar enforces that session re-validation occurs on every state-changing request (POST/PUT/DELETE) by injecting a X-Vault-Session-Epoch header that the application's OncePerRequestFilter validates against the current epoch window. A forged cross-origin request cannot include this header due to CORS preflight (the ALB has a listener rule that returns 403 for any request to /api/admin/* lacking the X-Vault-Session-Epoch header with a value matching the current 60-second window).
